title: [TEST COPY] Multisensory Gamma Entrainment
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a single healthy participant (23-year-old male) investigating gamma-band brain entrainment in response to different sensory modalities. The study examines auditory (5 kHz carrier tone amplitude-modulated at 40 Hz), visual (20 Hz flickering light), and combined audio-visual stimulation, each presented for 40 seconds. The research aims to characterize how multimodal sensory stimulation produces synchronized brain oscillations.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 19 monopolar channels using the standard 10/20 system referenced to earlobes at 500 Hz sampling rate with electrode impedance maintained below 20 kOhm. Auditory stimulation consisted of a 5 kHz carrier tone amplitude-modulated with a 40 Hz rectangular wave (4% duty cycle). Visual stimulation was a 20 Hz flickering white LED array at 50 cm distance. Preprocessing followed Makoto's pipeline including highpass filtering (>1 Hz), line noise removal, bad channel rejection and interpolation, average re-referencing, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction, independent component analysis, dipole fitting, and bad dipole rejection using EEGLab.
